speakingObjectives: State that your partner has a severe shellfish allergy and that even a small amount causes a severe allergic reaction.
Ask whether the same fryer is used for the shrimp.
Ask whether the soup stock and sauce contain shellfish or shrimp, and ask the server to check with the kitchen.
Thank the server, then say you will eat somewhere else.

forms.label: Severe allergy statement
forms.japanese: パートナーには重度の貝類・甲殻類アレルギーがあります
forms.english: My partner has a severe shellfish allergy.
forms.explanation: に marks the person who has something, and は makes the partner the topic. が marks the allergy as the subject. あります is the polite form of ある, used here to say that the partner has an allergy.

forms.label: Shared fryer question
forms.japanese: エビと同じフライヤーを使っていますか
forms.english: Do you use the same fryer for the shrimp?
forms.explanation: エビと同じ means “the same as the shrimp.” を marks フライヤー as the object. 使っていますか politely asks about the restaurant’s usual practice: “Do you use it?”

forms.label: Polite request to check
forms.japanese: 厨房に確認していただけますか
forms.english: Could you check with the kitchen?
forms.explanation: 確認して is the て-form of 確認する (“check”). いただけますか makes a polite request, while 厨房に names the party—the kitchen staff—to check with.

speakingObjectives: Ask the server to explain the bread charge, seat charge, and service charge on the bill.
Say that you did not order the bread and that the service charge is not listed on the menu.
Agree to pay the seat charge of 300 yen per person and ask the server to correct the bill.
Pay the corrected total by card and ask for a receipt.

forms.label: Bread not ordered
forms.japanese: パンは頼んでいません
forms.english: I did not order the bread.
forms.explanation: は marks 'the bread' as the topic. 頼んでいません is the polite negative of 頼む (to order) in the ～ている form, meaning 'have not ordered'.

forms.label: Request to correct the bill
forms.japanese: 請求書を訂正していただけますか
forms.explanation: を marks 請求書 (the bill) as the object of 訂正する (“correct”). 訂正して is its て-form; いただけますか makes the request polite.

forms.label: Paying the corrected total by card
forms.japanese: 訂正後の合計をカードで払います
forms.english: I will pay the corrected total by card.
forms.explanation: 訂正後の合計 means “the total after correction.” を marks that total as the object of 払います (“pay”); カードで means “by card,” with で marking the payment method.

speakingObjectives: Ask the server how much the fish of the day costs.
Explain that you have a limited budget today.
Decline the suggested side dish and say you will keep your order.
Keep the original daily set meal, which includes soup and dessert.

forms.label: Asking the fish price
forms.japanese: 本日の魚料理はいくらですか
forms.english: How much is the fish of the day?
forms.explanation: いくら means 'how much'. は marks the fish as the topic, and ですか makes the polite question 'How much is ...?'

forms.label: Stating a limited budget
forms.japanese: 今日は予算が限られています
forms.english: I have a limited budget today.
forms.explanation: 今日は sets “today” as the topic. 予算が限られています uses the passive 限られる (“be limited”) plus 〜ている to describe the budget’s resulting state.

forms.label: Declining a side dish
forms.japanese: 付け合わせの追加はしません
forms.english: I will not add a side dish.
forms.explanation: 付け合わせの追加 means “adding a side dish.” は marks that addition as the topic or contrast; しません is the polite negative of する (“do”).
